title: Metric provenance: trace-linked KPI bridge for inference requests
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Build a lightweight bridge that links per-request inference KPIs (token latency, model selection, cache hit) to trace context without exploding metric cardinality. This enables root-cause analysis and SLO attribution: when a latency or error spike appears in Prometheus dashboards, engineers must be able to pivot to the exact set of traces and identifying attributes quickly.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Prometheus metrics emitted from inference runtime include exemplar references to OTLP trace IDs for a sampled subset (configurable sampling rate). 2) A Prometheus-to-OTel lookup utility (CLI + internal service) can accept a metric exemplar label and return the corresponding trace and span context within <5s. 3) Cardinality safeguards: trace_id is not added as a regular metric label; only exemplars or ephemeral lookup indices are used. 4) Dashboard drilldowns showing correlated metric spike -> trace list in Grafana exist for per-model and per-route KPIs. 5) Security: trace linking honors PII data handling rules and KMS-signed provenance tokens when required.
design_notes: - Approach: implement a small sidecar (metric-provenance-agent) co-located with runtime pods that performs exemplar injection and maintains a short-lived index mapping exemplar IDs to OTLP trace IDs and a minimal attribute set (route, model, tenant). - Use exemplars for trace linkage where supported (Prometheus 2.7+ / remote write exemplars), and fall back to a secure ephemeral index backed by Redis for Prometheus servers that drop exemplars. - Runtime will add a TraceHook interface allowing runtime code paths (request entry, cache lookup, kernel dispatch) to call into sidecar with (trace_context, small attribute bag) to produce an exemplar or index entry. - Sampling: deterministic sampling using tenant+request-hash to ensure reproducible capture for a fraction of requests; configurable per-tenant and per-route. - Cardinality limits: index TTL (default 1h), attribute whitelist enforced, and tokenized attribute hashing to avoid free-form label growth. - Security: index entries are encrypted at rest and require a signed short-lived token for lookup; security_review_required flagged for compliance review. - Observability: sidecar exposes its own internal metrics (index_size, exemplars_emitted, lookup_latency) and structured logs.
technical_decisions: 1) Use exemplars where possible instead of creating a trace_id label on every metric to avoid cardinality blowup. 2) Implement a small, language-agnostic sidecar so language runtimes (Go, Python, Rust) only need a tiny client lib for the TraceHook. 3) For environments that block exemplars (some managed Prometheus offerings), support a secure remote-write adapter that writes a compact provenance record to a separate high-throughput store with the same retention as exemplars TTL. 4) Deterministic sampling reduces noise for debugging while allowing targeted increases for customer-impact incidents. 5) All index records include a signature derived from KMS to prevent tampering during cross-region lookups.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike, 1 week): prototype sidecar that receives OTLP trace IDs and emits a Prometheus exemplar on a test runtime; spike also validates exemplar round-trip in our dev Prometheus. Phase 2 (core, 3 weeks): build sidecar + client lib, implement sampling config, secure index with encryption, unit+integration tests. Phase 3 (canary, 1 week): deploy to dedicated capacity staging and enable on selected internal routes; add Grafana panels and lookup tool. Phase 4 (rollout, 1 week): enable tenant opt-in and run a gradual ramp with monitor-based rollback. Phase 5 (follow-up, ongoing): tune sampling heuristics, add tenant quotas, and integrate with alerting playbooks.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: cardinality explosion if developers misuse trace fields as regular labels. Mitigation: client lib enforces exemplar-only APIs and lints at compile/test time; runtime integration test checks for forbidden label additions. Risk: managed Prometheus providers stripping exemplars. Mitigation: remote-write provenance channel and explicit doc for marketplace partners. Risk: PII leakage via attributes. Mitigation: attribute whitelist + hashing + security review. Risk: additional latency on hot paths. Mitigation: sidecar uses async buffered writes and a small bounded queue; metrics on sidecar latency to detect regressions.
dashboards_and_alerting: - New Grafana panels in runtime-kpis: 'Token latency with exemplar drilldown', 'Per-route error rate with linked traces', and 'Sidecar health & exemplar emission rate'. - Alerts: sidecar_queue_overflow (P0), exemplar_emission_drop (>5min), exemplar_lookup_latency > 2s. - On-call playbook link: confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Metric+Provenance+Playbook
test_plan: Unit tests for client lib, integration test for exemplar emission + trace lookup, chaos test simulating index eviction under pressure, performance test measuring added p50/p95 per-request latency at 99th percentile. Canary metrics: exemplar_emit_rate, runtime_p95_latency_delta, index_hit_rate.
rollout_plan: Start with internal tenants and non-critical routes for 48h canary. Monitor exemplar_emit_rate and runtime latency; if no regressions escalate to opt-in for pilot customers. Provide customers a toggle and per-tenant sampling knobs. Full default-on rollout only after security approval and two successful canaries.
